selected.context: At decision point D3, which position does this researcher hold?
selected.a: Uses a skeptical second-line stress-testing function that challenges load-bearing safety claims, while staying grounded in day-to-day work without becoming contributors who compromise independence.
selected.b: Distrusts behavior measured on a single training prompt, since RL can install non-robust heuristics that vanish under small prompt changes (e.g., swapping [ORG] for [ORG]), so robustness across prompt variations is required for a convincing result.

selected.context: At decision point D6, which position does this researcher hold?
selected.a: prefers disclosing the full research process (first environments built, no unreported ones, runs counted, a bug found) over presenting only clean results, because it lets readers judge selection effects.
selected.b: Prefers modest, scoped claims (proof of viability, simple baseline) over claiming the technique suffices for high-stakes oversight, because confident-but-wrong outcomes still occur.

selected.context: At decision point D3, which position does this researcher hold?
selected.a: Distrusts evaluation outcomes for models that can reason strategically without visible chain-of-thought, since they may identify an evaluation and steer its result.
selected.b: Prefers evidence of an ulterior motive that is internal or occurs in real or realistic situations over prompted or simulated behavior, because prompted results only test the model+prompt combination.

selected.context: At decision point D3, which position does this researcher hold?
selected.a: Distrusts surface-level safety testing that only checks whether AIs ever appear to behave badly, since models can appear well-behaved while harboring secret motives.
selected.b: Prefers a comparison against a stronger model given the same ground-truth data over raw accuracy as evidence, because it rules out the explanation that the answer is derivable from training data.

selected.context: At decision point D6, which position does this researcher hold?
selected.a: Prefers hedged, nuanced claims that acknowledge normative ambiguity and mixed effects over overclaiming, because some behaviors (deferring when challenged) are not clearly wrong.
selected.b: Treat single-setting results as modest evidence only; claim the methodology and building blocks transfer rather than the specific numbers or protocol rankings.

proposals.principle: Prefers a skeptical second-line stress-testing function that challenges load-bearing claims over close-in contributors, because independence from the work being evaluated keeps safety conclusions honest.
Prefers robustness-checked evidence over single-prompt results, because behaviors learned through RL can be brittle heuristics that vanish under small prompt changes.
Prefers modest, scoped claims such as proof of viability over claiming a technique suffices for high-stakes oversight, because confident-but-wrong outcomes still occur.
Prefers reporting conservative, limited conclusions over full process disclosure, because overstated scope is the bigger risk to readers than hidden selection effects.
Distrusts evaluation results from models that can reason strategically without visible chain-of-thought, because such models may recognize an evaluation and steer its outcome.
Prefers evidence of ulterior motives from internal or realistic situations over prompted or simulated behavior, because prompted results only reflect the model-plus-prompt combination.
Prefers skeptical safety testing that probes for hidden motives over surface-level checks of apparent good behavior, because models can look well-behaved while harboring secret goals.
Prefers comparison against a stronger model on the same ground-truth data over raw accuracy, because it rules out the explanation that answers are derivable from training data.
Prefers hedged, nuanced claims that acknowledge normative ambiguity and mixed effects over overclaiming, because some behaviors such as deferring when challenged are not clearly wrong.
Prefers treating single-setting results as modest evidence, because specific numbers and rankings may not transfer even when the methodology does.
